detail.longDescription: I was reading the seminal paper "Attention is All You Need" and I ran across the formula for attention: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) * V The "/sqrt(d_k)" got me curious: is there a rationale for implementing the FISR here because attention tends to be an intensive operation. Is there evidence a direct answer for this or rationally-inferable one based on public evidence for how LLMs are implemented?
